{"content": "## Creating a Google Cloud Compute Engine Instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

Below are two ways to create the instance:

1. **Using the `gcloud` CLI** (recommended for most users).
2. **Using the REST API** (for programmatic automation).

Both examples assume you have already:
- Enabled the Compute Engine API.
- Set up a project with billing enabled.
- Installed the Google Cloud SDK and authenticated with `gcloud auth login`.
- Selected a project with `gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID`.

> **Important:** The RTX A6000 GPU is only available in a handful of zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`). Check the [GPU availability page](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#available_zones) for your region.

---

### 1. `gcloud` CLI Command

```bash
# Replace placeholders with your own values
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # Zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
BOOT_DISK_SIZE_GB=100
BOOT_DISK_TYPE="pd-ssd"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance

gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project $PROJECT_ID \
  --zone $ZONE \
  --machine-type $MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family $IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project $IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size ${BOOT_DISK_SIZE_GB}GB \
  --boot-disk-type $BOOT_DISK_TYPE \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Optional: install CUDA toolkit if needed
# sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-1' \
  --tags http-server,https-server \
  --scopes compute-rw,storage-ro
```

**Explanation of key flags**:
- `--accelerator`: Adds the GPU to the instance.
- `--image-family` & `--image-project`: Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.
- `--metadata startup-script`: Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically after boot.
- `--tags`: Allows HTTP/HTTPS traffic if you plan to run a web server.
- `--scopes`: Grants the instance permissions to access Compute Engine and Cloud Storage.

After the instance boots, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh $INSTANCE_NAME@$ZONE 
# Inside the instance
nvidia-smi
```

---

### 2. REST API Call

Below is a sample JSON payload and `curl` command to create the same instance via the REST API. Replace placeholders accordingly.

```bash
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# JSON body
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API call (requires OAuth 2.0 access token)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

curl -X POST \ 
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d @instance.json
```

**Notes**:
- The `acceleratorType` field uses the fully-qualified resource name.
- The `metadata` section contains a `startup-script` that installs the NVIDIA driver.
- Ensure you have the necessary IAM permissions (`compute.instances.create`, `compute.disks.create`, etc.).

---

### Post‑Creation Steps

1. **Install NVIDIA drivers** (if not already done via startup script):
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
   sudo reboot
   ```
2. **Verify GPU**:
   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```
3. **Optional – Install CUDA Toolkit** (if you need GPU compute libraries):
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-1
   ```

---

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Instance fails to start | GPU quota exceeded | Request a quota increase via the Cloud Console. |
| `nvidia-smi` shows no GPU | Wrong GPU type or zone | Verify the zone supports RTX A6000 and that the accelerator was added correctly. |
| Driver installation fails | Outdated driver package | Use the latest driver version from NVIDIA or install via `apt-get install nvidia-driver-535`. |

---

**References**:
- [Google Cloud Compute Engine GPUs](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus)
- [Creating instances with GPUs](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/create-gpu-instance)
- [REST API reference for Instances](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/instances)

Happy computing!", "filename": "create-rtx-a6000-instance.md"}

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.
